title: Lisbon earthquake and tsunami, 1755

place.label: Epicentre at sea off Portugal
place.basis: NCEI published epicentre for event 1339, given to whole degrees; the true source is debated
place.coords_source: NOAA NCEI Significant Earthquake Database, event 1339

date.label: Earthquake date in the NCEI catalogue

facts.text: NCEI links this earthquake to a tsunami record.
The study reports that the tsunami climbed roughly 5 to 15 m up the shores of Portugal and Morocco, and that the Azores and Madeira also saw large waves.
Accounts from far across the Atlantic, from Caribbean islands, Brazil and Newfoundland, show the waves travelled the whole ocean.

claims.text: The earthquake was about magnitude 8.5 or larger.
Where the fault that broke lies.

positions.text: Simulations put the source south of Gorringe Bank, in the Horseshoe Plain area (2009 study).
The exact source is still uncertain; the Marquês de Pombal fault fitted the geologic record best (2021 study).

tiers.everyday: On 1 November 1755 a great earthquake struck under the Atlantic off Portugal. A study listed by USGS describes it as the most destructive quake Europe has known, and its tsunami reached coasts on both sides of the ocean.
tiers.student: NOAA NCEI lists magnitude 8.5 (Mw), intensity XI on the Modified Mercalli scale and 50,000 deaths, and links a tsunami. A 2009 study estimated Mw 8.5–9.0 and put the tsunami at about 5–15 m on the shores of Portugal and Morocco, with accounts from Caribbean islands, Brazil and Newfoundland. Where the fault lies is still debated.
